latest.question: Deputy Ken O'Flynn asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance the position of the Government on the European Commission's Savings and Investments Union Strategy and associated proposals, including the Commission's recommendation on savings and investment accounts; whether Ireland has sought or secured an opt out from any element of those proposals.
latest.reply:
Consideration of the proposed Investment Account is taking place in the context of the EU Savings and Investments Union project (SIU). The Savings and Investments Union (SIU) is a flagship project within EU financial services policy. It aims to deepen and further integrate Europe’s capital markets, support growth, and enhance the resilience of the financial system. SIU is the umbrella term for the Capital Market Union and the Banking Union, and it is initiative a key priority for this Commission’s legislative term.
The main aim of SIU is to help European citizens to invest more to ensure that they have better financial outcomes and are better provided for in the future. Furthermore, the project also seeks to deepen the pools of capital that can be made available for investment purposes to ultimately grow the European economy. In March 2025, the European Commission launched the SIU Strategy, which included discrete measures to advance the SIU project. From the outset, Ireland has been a strong supporter of the SIU and its objectives.
Since the publication of the SIU Strategy in March 2025, the European Commission has been active in bringing forward a number of legislative and non-legislative reforms that were announced in the Strategy, including reviews of the Securitisation Framework and the Supplementary Pensions Framework as well as the Market Integration and Supervision Package.

latest.question: Deputy Darren O'Rourke asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance the estimated full year costs of increasing the standard rate income tax band available to recipients of the single person child carer credit from €48,000 to €51,750; and the estimated cost of increasing the value of the single person child carer credit from €1,900 to €2,100.
latest.reply:
As the Deputy may be aware, the pre-Budget 2027 Ready Reckoner is available on the Revenue Statistics webpage at:
www.revenue.ie/en/corporate/documents/statistics/ready-reckoner.pdf.
The Ready Reckoner shows a wide range of detailed information, including the estimated cost to the Exchequer of increasing the Single Person Child Carer Credit (SPCCC). Amounts other than those shown can be extrapolated using a straight line or pro-rata calculation. However, for the Deputy’s convenience the table below provides for the estimate cost of increasing the SPCCC as proposed by the Deputy.
Turning to Deputy’s proposal to increase the additional standard rate cut-off point for those qualifying for the SPCCC , I am advised by Revenue that the estimated full-year cost to the Exchequer is €23 million.
These costs are estimates for 2027 based on Revenue’s micro-simulation tool, Tax Modeller, using actual data for the latest year available, currently 2024, adjusted for income and employment trends in the interim.

latest.question: Deputy Cathal Crowe asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance if consideration has been given to the policy of introducing a personal tax credit for people with a disability in employment.
latest.reply:
The Government recognises the significant financial pressures experienced by households with disabilities, particularly amid the heightened cost?of?living conditions of recent years. In response, we have implemented targeted budget measures designed to support those most vulnerable.
When this Government took office, we committed to a step change in the delivery of supports and services for people with disability and their families, in line with our Programme for Government commitments.
There are currently a number of tax measures within the tax system that support people with disabilities and carers, this includes Tax Relief for Health Expenses which provides relief to individuals who have incurred costs in respect of qualifying health expenses and the Blind Person’s Tax Credit, which is available to a blind person or a person who has impaired vision.
There are more than 346,000 people with disabilities in Ireland who are already in work. They are contributing to our economy, supporting their families and communities, and making an enormous contribution to our country.
Recognising there is a significant gap in participation, over the course of the next year, the Government is committed to examining what further measures can be taken to recognise the contribution of those who are already working while doing more to remove the barriers faced by those who want to enter or remain in employment.

latest.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance the number of individual taxpayers who have paid tax as a result of the so-called "deemed disposal" rule in relation to exchange traded funds in each year since it was introduced; and the total tax revenue generated in each year.
latest.reply:
The information available to Revenue does not allow them to isolate the tax returned due to the deemed disposal rule from other chargeable events which give rise to a tax liability. Chargeable events include:
• the making of relevant payments;
• the redemption of the investment;
• the transfer by an investor of their investment; and
• the ending of an eight-year period following the acquisition of the investment and then every eight years thereafter (deemed disposal).
Therefore, it is not possible to directly identify the tax revenue arising from the application of the deemed disposal rule. This is because investment funds and life companies are not obliged to report the category of chargeable event that the exit tax relates to at the time of making payment to Revenue. Similarly, as respects investments in certain Irish domiciled funds and offshore funds in respect of which investors are required to self-assess tax due, taxpayers are not required to separately report data for each category of chargeable event when filing their tax return.

latest.question: Deputy Peter 'Chap' Cleere asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance if he will clarify whether new tax exemptions or incentives that are being introduced to encourage personal savings and investment will also apply to individuals who have already established savings or investment policies; if existing investments will be eligible for the same tax treatment as new investments.
latest.reply:
Encouraging retail investment remains a key priority of mine. As the Deputy is aware, Budget 2026 included a commitment to publish a Roadmap: ‘Taxation of Retail Investment – A New Path Forward for Ireland’, setting out the intended approach to simplify and adapt the tax framework to encourage retail investment while retaining necessary and important anti-avoidance protections, in a proportionate manner.
The Roadmap was published on 31 August.
A key aspect of the Roadmap is the inclusion of key parameters of the proposed new investment account, acknowledging the need for industry to understand how the account is intended to operate. This information is to facilitate the design and introduction of the necessary operational systems by providers, to allow accounts to be available in 2027, with the specific details of the investment account forming part of the normal budgetary process, in October 2026. The intention is to legislate for the account in 2026 and to allow accounts to be offered in 2027.
As mentioned in the Roadmap, the current taxation regime for retail investment, including the deemed disposal rule, will not apply to the new account.
The key features of the proposed investment account are as follows:
• Taxed account, with tax applying annually at a low flat tax rate (%) to the value of the account above a tax-free threshold.
• No minimum contribution requirement.
• Maximum annual contribution limit.
• One account per person.

latest.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport if his Department has examined the barriers faced by students from the Erris region of County Mayo in accessing third-level education due to the lack of direct public transport services to major education centres including Galway and Limerick:.
latest.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for policy and overall funding in relation to public transport; however, I am not involved in the day-to-day operations of public transport. The National Transport Authority (NTA) has statutory responsibility for securing the provision of public passenger transport services nationally and for the scheduling and timetabling of these services in conjunction with the relevant transport operators.
We are at a key juncture for public transport in Ireland. Reliable and sustainable services are critical as passenger numbers grow, congestion worsens in urban areas, and a greater proportion of the population depends on public transport for commuting, education, and essential travel.
The NTA is managing the 2026 allocation by prioritising delivery of existing programmes in line with operational readiness and resources. Enhancements within the current allocation are prioritised, some changes are cost-neutral, while others require additional resources, and all are subject to funding, readiness, and capacity.
Transport planning and strategic decision-making are guided by a balanced assessment of operational and resource considerations. These decisions are also made following operational and performance analysis of existing services, including customer feedback.

latest.question: Deputy Barry Ward asked the Minister for Transport If his attention has been drawn to the actions of the French government which has introduced a specific penalty of €100 per tonne for non-compliance with CORSIA offsetting obligations together with the possibility of an operating ban; whether the Government will introduce an equivalent national penalty for non-compliance with CORSIA that is consistent with the excess emissions penalty applicable under the EU ETS, in order to ensure that Irish airlines operate on a level playing field with competitors in other Member States and to support the integrity of multilateral climate action.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 92 and 93 together.
The Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) was adopted by ICAO in 2016 as a global market-based measure to address CO? emissions from international aviation. The scheme requires airlines to offset emissions above an agreed baseline and is being implemented in three phases: a Pilot Phase (2021-2023), Phase I (2024-2026) and Phase II (2027-2035). Participation is voluntary during the first two phases, while from 2027 the scheme will apply more broadly, subject to certain exemptions, including for Least Developed Countries, Small Island Developing States and Landlocked Developing Countries. Ireland, together with all EU Member States, has participated in CORSIA since its commencement. Participation has continued to expand, with 130 States participating in the scheme from 1 January 2026.
CORSIA enters Phase II from 1 January 2027 during which participation will be determined based on 2018 Revenue Tonne Kilometres (RTK) data. As a result, participation is anticipated to expand further to 134 States as Brazil, China, India and the Russian Federation will come into scope for participation.
Within the EU, both CORSIA and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) are implemented through Directive 2003/87/EC. latest.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Transport if he will contact Irish Rail on a matter (details supplied).
latest.reply:
As Minister of State, I have responsibility for International and Road Transport, Logistics, Rail and Ports; however, I am not involved in the day-to-day operations of public transport.
The query raised by the Deputy is an operational matter for Iarnród Éireann. I have, therefore, referred the Deputy's question to the company for direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within ten working days.

latest.question: Deputy Duncan Smith asked the Minister for Transport to provide an update on the provision of new rail carriages for the Northern Commuter line; when these carriages will be operational; and the extra capacity these carriages will provide.
latest.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for policy and overall funding in relation to public transport. Under the Dublin Transport Authority Act 2008, the National Transport Authority (NTA) has statutory responsibility for the provision of public transport infrastructure and services within the Greater Dublin Area.
With regard to the Deputy's specific questions regarding provision of new rail carriages, this is a matter for the NTA and I have forwarded the Deputy's questions to the NTA for a more detailed reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a response within 10 working days.
Pending this more detailed response, three fleet orders have been placed under the DART+ programme, comprising 285 carriagtes in total. The first order for the purchase of 95 additional DART carriages (65 battery-electric and 30 electric) are currently undergoing certification and safety testing. It is intended that the new battery-electric sets will be initially deployed on the Northern Commuter Line serving Dublin to/from Drogheda from 2027. The installation of charging infrastructure in Drogheda to facilitate this service enhancement is complete with testing ongoing.

latest.question: Deputy Sorca Clarke asked the Minister for Transport for an update in relation to the current status of the Iarnród Éireann National Carpark Strategy report which is currently bring reviewed with the NTA; and when this report will be published.
latest.reply:
As Minister of Transport, I have responsibility for policy and overall funding of public transport. The operation, maintenance and renewal of the rail network and stations on the network, including the Iarnród Éireann National Carpark Strategy report, is a matter for Iarnród Éireann in the first instance.
Given Iarnród Éireann's responsibility in this matter, I have referred the Deputy's question to the company for direct, detailed reply. Please contact my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.

latest.question: Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Transport to outline the State's policy toward supporting electric buses and the development of a charging infrastructure nationwide.
latest.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for policy and overall funding in relation to public transport. The National Transport Authority (NTA) has statutory responsibility for the planning and development of public transport infrastructure, including the provision and upgrade of public bus fleets and bus depots.
Noting the NTA's responsibility in the matter, I have referred the Deputy's question to the NTA for a direct reply. Please contact my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
Pending this detailed response, over 250 battery-electric buses have been accepted into the Dublin Bus and Bus Éireann fleets across the country, with fully electric services now in operation in Limerick and Athlone. The electrification of the bus fleet is a key part of the BusConnects programmes and in our investment in public transport across the country more generally, helping to make a sustainable mode of travel even more sustainable.
The NTA has recently awarded a new national electric bus charging infrastructure framework which will allow suppliers to be accessed for depot electrification projects anywhere in the country and will replace the fragmented, project-by-project procurement approach to date.

examples.question: Deputy Paul McAuliffe asked the Minister for Social Protection the eligibility of a person (details supplied) for a pension (non-contributory).
examples.reply:
An application for State pension non-contributory was received from the person concerned on 10 September 2024.
The maximum weekly rate of pension was awarded with effect from 19 September 2024 and notification of the decision issued, in writing, on 16 September 2024.
I hope this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Emer Currie asked the Minister for Education and Youth the position regarding a project (details supplied).
examples.reply:
As previously advised to the Deputy, the school referred to was approved to enter my Department's pipeline of projects under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme.
The project received approval from my Department to commence construction in January 2026. More recently, Department officials were notified by the school authorities that construction has now commenced. Expected completion to coincide with the start of the new school year.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Pa Daly asked the Minister for Health the total number of GPs, and the number of GPs providing GMS services, in County Kerry, by local health area and per 10,000 population, at 1 December for each year from 2020 to 2025, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
As this is a service matter, I have asked the HSE to reply to the Deputy directly as soon as possible.
Please note that as GPs are private practitioners, accordingly it may only be possible for the HSE to respond in relation to HSE contracted GPs.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.

examples.reply:
The table below outlines the payroll costs of my Department from 2015-2025.

As this question also relates to agencies under the remit of the Department of Transport, I have referred the question to these agencies to reply to you directly. If the Deputy does not receive a response within ten working days, please contact my Private Office.
